Cowell's shaped noteheads (diamond = 7 per bar, triangle = 3 per bar, square = 9 per bar) are written as plain tuplets: diamond voice \tuplet 7/4 eighths (m10, m12), triangle voice \tuplet 3/2 half+quarter (m10, m12) and triplet eighths (m11 top), square bass \tuplet 9/8 sixteenths (m10, m11). No nested tuplets needed (and the grammar would drop a \tuplet inside a \tuplet: tuplet_event filters inner events to note/rest/context). Not expressible: the special notehead shapes; hiding tuplet numbers/brackets (the original prints none; only TimeSignature/BarLine can be \omit-ted); the tie into F#4 from bar 9 and the slur out of m12 C5 into bar 13; parenthesized courtesy naturals (F5 and F3 m10, A2 and C5 m11) are not drawn since there is no earlier in-bar accidental. Accidentals carried in-bar per standard convention: m11 bass last note C#4, m12 bass last note F#3 (printed with no accidental).
